# Mercury HTTP Server

> Lightweight, high-performance, configurable HTTP/1.1 server implemented in C++20 for Linux and Windows.

- **Website**: https://mercury.wowtravis.com/
- **Repository**: https://github.com/travis-heavener/mercury
- **Releases**: https://github.com/travis-heavener/mercury/releases
- **Release Metadata**: https://mercury.wowtravis.com/releases.json

## Quick Overview
Mercury is a standalone C++20 web server engineered for low memory utilization (~9MB idle on Linux) with sub-millisecond static response times.
Features: HTTP/1.1 (w/ HTTP/1.0 & 0.9 compatibility), TLS 1.3 (OpenSSL), streaming compression (Brotli, Zstandard, Gzip, Deflate), RFC 3875 Fast CGI (PHP), IP access control, regex URL rewriting, and HTTP redirects.

## Downloading Pre-compiled Releases
Pre-compiled 64-bit binaries are available on GitHub Releases:
- **Windows (x64)**: `Windows_<VERSION>.zip` (e.g. `Windows_v0_35_0.zip`)
  - Standalone `bin/mercury.exe` with zero external runtime DLL dependencies.
- **Linux (x64)**: `Linux_<VERSION>.tar.gz` (e.g. `Linux_v0_35_0.tar.gz`)
  - Standalone `bin/mercury` built on Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35+; supports APT, Pacman, DNF).
  - *Note*: Releases v0.28.4–v0.29.2 use prefix `Debian_` instead of `Linux_`.
- **Integrity**: Compare download digests against SHA-256 hashes listed in `releases.json`.

Download URL format:
`https://github.com/travis-heavener/mercury/releases/download/<VERSION>/<FILENAME>`

## Running Mercury
```bash
# Linux
./bin/mercury [options]

# Windows
bin\mercury.exe [options]
```

Common CLI options:
- `-c, --config <file>`: Configuration path (default: `conf/mercury.conf`)
- `-p, --port <port>`: Override HTTP port (default: `80`)
- `-r, --root <path>`: Override document root directory (default: `public/`)
- `-t, --test`: Test configuration file syntax and exit
- `-v, --version`: Display version information
- `-h, --help`: Display usage and options

Interactive console commands (available while running):
`help`, `status`, `info`, `pwd`, `ping`, `phpinit`, `clear`, `exit`.

## Building from Source
Prerequisites: GCC (C++20), Make, NASM, UPX, and OpenSSL. Windows builds cross-compile from Linux using MinGW-w64 (`x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++`).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/travis-heavener/mercury.git && cd mercury
make clean                 # Clean prior artifacts
make lib_deps              # Install system build dependencies (APT, Pacman, DNF)

# Linux build:
make libs -j LINUX_ONLY=1  # Build static dependencies (omit Windows libs)
make linux                 # Produces bin/mercury

# Windows build (cross-compiled via MinGW-w64):
make libs -j               # Build all static dependencies (includes Windows libs)
make windows               # Produces bin/mercury.exe

# Build both:
make libs -j && make all   # Produces bin/mercury and bin/mercury.exe
```

## Configuration
Mercury uses XML configuration files. A default template is provided in `conf/default/mercury.conf`.
- At runtime, Mercury defaults to loading `conf/mercury.conf` (or a custom path via `-c, --config`).
- Comprehensive documentation for all configuration directives and accepted values is maintained in `CONFIG.md`.
